description_full: SCHOTT Pharma AG & Co. KGaA develops, manufactures, and sells drug containment solutions and delivery systems for injectable drugs for pharma, biotech, and life science industries worldwide. The company offers syriQ, a glass syringe for vaccines; syriQ BioPure, a glass syringe for biologics; syriQ BioPure silicone-free, a prefillable and silicone-free glass syringe for biologics; SCHOTT TOPPAC, a polymer syringe; SCHOTT TOPPAC cosmetic, a polymer syringe for aesthetic treatments; SCHOTT TOPPAC freeze, a polymer syringe for deep-cold applications; SCHOTT TOPPAC sensitive, a polymer syringe for sensitive drugs; SCHOTT TOPPAC infuse, a polymer syringe for infusion therapy; SCHOTT TOPPAC unique, a polymer container; and SCHOTT TOPPAC cartridge. It also provides pharmaceutical glass cartridge, such as cartriQ for peptide and protein-based injectables; cartriQ Large Volume for large-volume injectables; Cartridges Double Chamber for lyophilized drugs; Cartridges Break Resistant; and TopLine and StandardLine cartridges and vials. In addition, the company offers pharmaceutical glass vial, including adaptiQ for injectables; EVERIC pure for unmatched drug stability; EVERIC freeze for deep-cold applications; EVERIC care for a pH range; EVERIC strong & smooth for the filling line performance; EVERIC smart; EVERIC plus for sensitive drug formulations; and EVERIC Iyo to avoid fogging for lyophilized drugs. Further, it provides pharmaceutical glass ampoule products, comprising Ampoules easyOPC for ampoule opening; Ampoules Anti-Counterfeiting for protection against drug counterfeiting; and StandardLine ampoules. It also provides containment and drug delivery, analytics, fill-and-finish, regulatory, and sustainability services. The company was founded in 1884 and is headquartered in Mainz, Germany. SCHOTT Pharma AG & Co. KGaA operates as a subsidiary of Schott Glaswerke Beteiligungs- Und Export Gmbh.

financial_summary: SCHOTT Pharma AG & Co. KGaA is a mid-cap healthcare business with a $3.9B market cap on $1.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +7% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 21% against a 10% cost of capital — a 11-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 34%.

The business throws off $39M in free cash flow — roughly 4 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.23× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.2× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 9.3×.
Shareholder yield is only 0.7%, a thin return of capital, and within its sector the business captures 2.2× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 13% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has rebounded 50% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 14% below the high.

val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $3.66 (margin of safety -79%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 8%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $2.58 to $5.32 (P10-P90).

Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 1.0% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.0% (vs the 8% bar).
The price implies 16.3% annual cash-flow growth, 10pp more than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 21% clears the cost of capital of 10.0% by 11pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.11).
It runs a 34% gross margin and converts 4% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.23x.
ROE of 16% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.8x equity multiplier).
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.2x net debt to EBITDA ($28.6M of cash against $92.5M of debt), with interest covered 9.3x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 4.2, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 7.0% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 20.8% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
own: Shareholder yield is a modest 0.7% (0.8% in dividends).
people: With about 5,002 employees, each generates about $220K of revenue, 0.6x the Healthcare median.
That works out to $8K of free cash flow per employee.
